courses.title: Caro-Kann Foundations
courses.summary: Five short sessions on the Caro-Kann's main lines, its structures and the sharpest ways White attacks it.

days.title: The main lines at a glance
days.takeaway: 1...c6 prepares ...d5, so Black challenges e4 with a pawn behind it. The Classical ...Bf5, the Karpov ...Nd7 and the ...Nf6 lines all grow from the same 3.Nc3 dxe4 4.Nxe4 position.

days.title: Advance, Fantasy, Exchange and Panov
days.takeaway: White's main ways to sidestep the Classical lines are 3.e5, 3.f3 and the exchange on d5, often followed by c4 in the Panov. Each one hands you a different pawn structure, and the structure tells you the plan.

days.title: What the Caro-Kann is really about

courses.title: Sicilian Essentials
courses.summary: Understand why 1...c5 works, which variation you're in, and how to handle the anti-Sicilians club players love.

days.title: Why 1...c5 works
days.takeaway: 1...c5 fights for d4 from the flank. In the Open Sicilian, Black trades the c-pawn for White's d-pawn and keeps an extra central pawn, an edge that often counts later in the game.

days.title: The anti-Sicilians
days.takeaway: Plenty of club opponents skip the Open Sicilian with 2.Nc3, 2.c3, 2.f4 or the Smith-Morra Gambit. Have a simple, confident answer ready for each one.

days.title: Every main variation in one sitting

courses.title: French Defense: Plans and Traps
courses.summary: The French's core ideas, its main variations from Black's side, and the traps that decide club games.

days.title: The French in one idea
days.takeaway: 1...e6 builds a solid centre but locks in the c8-bishop, so finding that bishop a job is a theme you'll meet again and again. Smirnov also flags early traps for both sides.

days.title: The Advance Variation and Black's middlegame plan
days.takeaway: After 3.e5, Black has a standard middlegame plan. This session maps it out and covers White's common tries, including a3 to stop ...Nb4.

courses.title: The Italian Game, Club Edition
courses.summary: Plans, sidelines and traps in the Italian from both sides of the board, from Black's gambits to the Fried Liver.

days.title: Basic ideas and Black's tricky sidelines
days.takeaway: Starting plans for both sides, then the sidelines club players love: the Paris Defense, Légal's mate, the Blackburne Shilling Gambit and the Rousseau Gambit.

days.title: Giuoco Piano with c3 and d4
days.takeaway: Why White plays 4.c3: it prepares d4 and the Center Attack. Includes a nine-move trap and a natural-looking queen move to avoid.

days.title: The slow Italian from Black's side
Two Knights and the Fried Liver

courses.title: London System Model Games
courses.summary: IM Eric Rosen's London System games to know by heart, with the traps that win club games.

days.title: Why the London, and a bullet masterclass
days.takeaway: Rosen makes his case for the London System, then walks through a fast game to show how the setup plays when the clock is short.

days.title: Kamsky's classic trap
days.takeaway: A London game from Gata Kamsky against Sam Shankland (2014), built around a trap worth knowing by heart.

courses.title: Scandinavian Defense Explained
courses.summary: Jonathan Schrantz on 1.e4 d5: the main lines, where the queen belongs, and top-level games in the opening.

days.title: 1.e4 d5 and the main line
days.takeaway: After 2.exd5 Qxd5 the black queen is out early, and the whole opening turns on where it goes next. Start with the main line.

days.title: Modern lines and alternatives
days.takeaway: A survey of the modern alternatives to the main line, so a deviation on move three or four doesn't leave you guessing.

days.title: A model game at the top

courses.title: Stop Hanging Pieces
courses.summary: Real positions where pieces get left hanging, and a short checklist that keeps yours protected.

days.title: Positions 1 to 3
days.takeaway: Dr. Can sorts hung pieces into three common kinds of blunder. Pause on each position and find the loose piece before he does.

days.title: Positions 4 and 5
days.takeaway: Two more positions. As you watch, name which of the three blunder types each one shows; naming the pattern is how you start catching it at the board.

courses.title: Avoid Knight Forks
courses.summary: Six practical tips from GM Igor Smirnov for keeping your pieces out of fork range, and for fighting back when one lands.

days.title: Tips 1 to 3
days.takeaway: Forks rarely come from nowhere; they follow a threat you didn't notice. The first three tips cover the knight patterns that set them up.

days.title: Tip 4 and a very common fork
days.takeaway: Tip 4, a fork blunder more than two million players have made, and how to start saving the game once you've been forked.

courses.title: The Power of the Pin
courses.summary: ChessNetwork's lesson on pins from both sides: why they bite, how to handle being pinned, and how to use one well.

days.title: What makes a pin powerful
days.takeaway: How pins work, which pieces can pin, and the first steps for handling a pin against you.

days.title: Strategic tips for pins
days.takeaway: Practical advice for both situations: when you're stuck in a pin, and when your opponent is.

courses.title: Discovered Attacks and Double Checks
courses.summary: Learn to see discovered attacks, discovered checks and double checks, so you stop missing them in your own games.

days.title: The concept and first examples
days.takeaway: A discovered attack happens when one piece moves out of the way and uncovers another's attack, so two threats land at once. Start with the idea and simple examples.

days.title: Building one from scratch
days.takeaway: How to set up a discovered attack when it isn't there yet, including removing the defender, then a harder final puzzle.

courses.title: What to Do in the Opening
courses.summary: Build a combative pawn structure and develop efficiently, with ChessNetwork's opening fundamentals.

days.title: Basic opening ideas
days.takeaway: The opening checklist in its simplest form, aimed at players who know the rules and want a starting plan.

days.title: The pawn duo
days.takeaway: The opening is about building a combative structure and developing efficiently. Two pawns side by side in the centre, a pawn duo, are the backbone of that structure.

courses.title: Blunder-Check Habits
courses.summary: Why middlegame blunders happen (focus, time, tunnel vision, overcomplicating) and the habits that stop them.

days.title: What counts as a blunder
days.takeaway: A real game full of mistakes, then a working definition of a blunder. Knowing what you're trying to prevent is step one.

days.title: Focus and the clock
days.takeaway: The first two causes: losing focus, and time trouble. Studer gives concrete do's and don'ts for playing with focus.

courses.title: Rook Endgame Essentials
courses.summary: The five rook-and-pawn positions every club player should know, one short lesson at a time.

days.title: The Lucena position
days.takeaway: The standard winning method with rook and pawn against rook: cut off the enemy king, then build a bridge with your rook to shelter your own king from checks.

days.title: The Philidor position
days.takeaway: The defender's first resource. Learn the common ways to get it wrong, then the correct method for holding the draw.

courses.title: King and Pawn Endgames
courses.summary: Opposition, shouldering and the decision to trade into a pawn ending, the basics that decide close games.

days.title: King and pawn vs king: the rules
days.takeaway: Common errors, then the basic evaluation. Opposition: the kings face each other on the same file with an odd number of squares between them, and it's the other side to move.

days.title: Winning paths and distant opposition
days.takeaway: Correcting the winning path, taking the opposition from a distance, and the exceptions to the rule.

days.title: Think before you trade into a pawn ending
